title: AMD CEO Lisa Su Sees AI Inference Boom Fueling $1.5T Demand By 2030: 'About 60% Of The Market Going Forward'
key_facts: Lisa Su, chief executive of AMD (Advanced Micro Devices), spoke at the 2026 OCP Global Summit.
She said 'This year is really the year of inference' and that inference (running AI models for users) is now about 60% of the AI market.
AMD expects the market for data-centre AI accelerators to approach $1.5 trillion by 2030.
She expects server processor (CPU) demand to grow about 50% a year over four or five years to over $200 billion by 2030, and said AMD has raised this estimate three times in nine months.

AMD's Helios rack-scale system, introduced in July, began production shipments in September to major customers including Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and Anthropic; production is to rise through the fourth quarter and into the first half of 2027.
Helios combines 72 GPUs and AMD estimates 30% more tokens per dollar; AMD also introduced Helion, a rack for agentic AI, and the EPYC Verano server chip.
All the market sizes are AMD's own estimates.

why_it_matters_hint: A chip maker's own forecast shows how big the data-centre build-out could become and where it expects demand to move.
event_date: 2026 OCP Global Summit; reported Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 (date of the talk not stated).
